note: Not a URL problem: the court's own site is reachable and readable now (the prior pass's CONNECT 403 is gone). Two separate things stop the curated name "U.S. Court of Appeals for the 2nd Circuit", and both are the name. (1) The project's own matcher refuses it before any fetch: uncheckable_reason() returns 'curated_count_label' because the token '2nd' carries a digit, so verify_base_graph.py will record 'not_checkable' and never fetch anything for this node. (2) Independently, the court does not write its name that way. www.ca2.uscourts.gov labels itself "United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit" in content (its page title is "United States Court of Appeals 2nd Circuit", which still omits the graph's "for the"). A curator renaming this node to "U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit" fixes both at once, and the same rename applies to all seven numbered circuits in this shard.

note: GPO renamed its business units and says so on its own site: "GPO has launched new names of its various business units... business units that are inward facing now start with the prefix 'Agency' whereas business units that are outward facing now start with the prefix 'Government'." The current unit corresponding to this node is named on gpo.gov's leadership page as "Managing Director of Government Secure & Intelligent Documents" — so GPO's own word is "Government Secure & Intelligent Documents", not the graph's "Security & Intelligent Documents", and the difference is enough to fail label equality (the fragment is a job title and 'of' is not one of the verifier's label separators). A curated rename, not a URL. GPO's full new-name list is at /docs/default-source/branding/gpo-business-unit-name-update-reference-guide.pdf, a PDF the label parser cannot read.

note: NSF's authoritative list of its own directorates and divisions was read and this division is not on it. The parent directorate has been renamed — the graph's "Education & Human Resources (EHR)" is now NSF's "Directorate for STEM Education (EDU)" — and that directorate's divisions are listed on the same page as exactly three: "Division of Graduate Education (EDU/DGE)", "Division of Research on Learning in Formal and Informal Settings (EDU/DRL)" and "Division of Undergraduate Education (EDU/DUE)". "Division of Human Resource Development" is not among them and appears nowhere on the page. Because this page is NSF's complete enumeration of its own divisions, the honest reading is that the curated node is stale, not that its page is missing; the fix is curation in CURATION.md, not another URL. https://www.nsf.gov/edu (3,328 chars) and https://www.nsf.gov/about (4,605 chars) were also read with the same result.

note: This is a real, statutorily named office and its name is not the problem — I simply cannot name a page for it. Four pages were read under the verifier's own policy and none names it, and more usefully none LINKS to it: https://www.house.gov/the-house-explained/officers-and-organizations (2,477 readable chars; names Chaplain, Sergeant at Arms, Chief Administrative Officer, General Counsel, Inspector General, Parliamentarian, Office of Congressional Conduct — the Attending Physician is absent from the House's own list of its officers and organizations), https://www.senate.gov/about/officers-staff.htm (4,936 chars), https://www.aoc.gov/what-we-do (2,203 chars). Fetching www.house.gov, www.senate.gov and www.aoc.gov and scanning their raw HTML for any href or text matching 'physician' returned zero hits on all three. https://www.senate.gov/reference/office/attending_physician.htm is a 404 served with status 200 (its title is "U.S. Senate: 404 Error Page"). oap.house.gov does not resolve (tunnel 502). The office is shared between the chambers and appears to publish nothing; if a page exists it is most likely behind the House/Senate intranet.

Verified against the curated file rather than assumed: "VA Medical Centers" is one node repeated under 18 different VISNs (exec-dept-va-vha-visn-1-new-england-vamc ... -visn-23-midwest-vamc), with the same name and the same structural description. It is the graph's per-VISN template placeholder, not a body VA names inside VISN 19. Two probes: https://www.va.gov/directory/guide/home.asp reads (1,766 chars) and does not label it; https://www.visn19.va.gov/ is refused because its robots.txt could not be reached, which this project treats as a complete disallow. I deliberately did NOT go hunting for a va.gov page that labels the generic phrase "VA medical centers": one such label would confirm all 18 of these template nodes from a single generic phrase, which is the same manufactured-confirmation failure this project already refuses for Inspector General links in agency footers. The curation fix is either real per-VISN facility nodes or dropping the placeholder.
